selection.course_codes: Stage 5 procedure unchanged: random.Random(20261009).sample of 12 codes per yearbook from module-description chunks (title + 'This/The module/course ...'), excluding Stage 4 codes, all 24 Stage 5 sampled codes (including spares) and codes whose description titles differ. First 5 per book -> exact code (interleaved Hum/Sci as E1..E10), next 5 -> code in context (Hum -> C1..C5, Sci -> C6..C10), 2 spares per book (unused: MHRM745, MAEHD504, GS201, GS212)
selection.question_forms: Exact-code wording reuses the Stage 5 E1..E10 templates in the same order. Code-in-context questions reuse the Stage 5 C1..C10 templates in the same order, so table-answer questions sit in the same positions as Stage 5 (C2, C5, C6, C9). Stage 5 did not record this position rule; it is fixed here before any retrieval run
selection.natural_language_topics: Stage 5 procedure unchanged: random.Random(20261009).sample from the 142 numbered section headings on pages <= 200 (Stage 4 topics excluded by the Stage 5 regex; the 10 Stage 5 topics excluded), taken in sample order, skipping (a) department/faculty names and learning-outcome bullets, (b) more than 2 postgraduate-research (MPhil/PhD) topics, (c) headings with no substantive section text. Skipped: #9 'Department of Crop Production and Horticulture' (rule a). Used: sample positions 1-8, 10, 11
selection.out_of_scope: Five questions in the Stage 5 style (general knowledge / campus life not covered by the yearbooks), each checked by plain text search
selection.answer_pages_found_by: plain text search of the chunk text for each section's or code's distinctive wording - no retriever used

grading: 2 = chunk alone is sufficient for an LLM to answer correctly; 1 = relevant but insufficient; 0 = irrelevant

questions.question: When can a PhD or MPhil student apply for full registration?
questions.sufficient: At the end of the provisional registration period, provided the candidate has successfully presented their final supervised proposal at a scheduled Faculty, School or Institute Seminar Series (otherwise extension or termination may be recommended)

questions.question: How early must I submit my master's dissertation proposal for approval?
questions.sufficient: To the appropriate department not less than six months before the completion of the dissertation; once approved it may not be changed without Senate permission

questions.question: What do I need to do to be allowed to sit the exam for a module?
questions.sufficient: Attend all lectures, tutorials, seminars and practical work and do the approved activities/assignments, and meet the department's (Senate-approved) requirements for the module; otherwise the student may not take that module's examination

questions.question: Can the university refuse to admit someone because of their religion or race?
questions.sufficient: No test of religious or political belief, race, ethnic origin, nationality or gender may be imposed for admission as staff or student or to hold office; the University may still give preference to citizens or residents of Zimbabwe

questions.question: What is included in a lecturer's annual performance report?
questions.sufficient: An assessment of the member's teaching, research, innovation and industrialisation (items 7.4 and 7.5), with an additional section for innovation, consultancy, creative work and enterprise development; placed in the personal file by the Head/Chairperson of Department

questions.question: Who sits on the university's Finance Committee?
questions.sufficient: Every Pro-Vice-Chancellor; 3 Council members who are not staff (one is Chairperson); 2 persons appointed by Senate; the Bursar (secretary); the Registrar; a representative of the deans appointed by Council

questions.question: What is work-related learning?
questions.sufficient: A prescribed period of hands-on practical experience in a relevant industrial, commercial/professional or community setting (Hum 122), or supervised work-related learning of normally at least ten months during the third level (Hum 136)

questions.question: How is an honours degree programme structured?
questions.sufficient: The main structural elements: one or more major modules studied over at least six or ten semesters, normally a period of work-related learning in the third level, modules studied intensively and progressively (structure prescribed in Special Faculty Regulations); later elements (project/dissertation, focused module combinations) alone are grade 1

questions.question: When does a Council member lose their seat?
questions.sufficient: A member vacates office (a) after resigning with the required notice, (b) on starting a prison sentence of 6 months or more without the option of a fine, (c) if disqualified under section 12(a)/(b), (d) if absent without permission from three consecutive Council meetings. Grade 2 for a chunk with at least three of the four grounds; fewer is grade 1
questions.note: answer split across chunks (Hum 18 chunk has (a)-(b); Sci 18 chunk has (a)-(c))

questions.question: I'm an older applicant without the normal entry qualifications. What do I need to get into a bachelor's degree?
questions.sufficient: Mature Entry: at least 25 (males) / 23 (females) on the first day of the academic year and not eligible under Normal or Special Entry; at least five approved O Levels including English Language and Mathematics (where required) or equivalents; demonstrated suitability through attainments/work experience. Programme-specific mature-entry rules (e.g. Hum 190) are grade 1
